scope: governance only; no domain design; introduces no requirement absent from the document

reviewed_baseline.note: No authoritative baseline exists. Nothing may be described as unchanged since review. A baseline is established only at merge, from records outside this pull request. Neither null nor an empty string is ever a valid baseline.

proof_classes.name: change detection
proof_classes.proves: unchanged against an externally bound baseline

proof_classes.name: semantic authority
proof_classes.proves: the content means what it should

authority_root: git immutable commit and tree identity
the GitHub review and merge record
an independent reviewer verdict on the complete diff at an exact head
validator_non_goals: judging whether a normative sentence is true
judging whether a mapping is semantically sound
standing in for a reviewer or a Founder decision
proving that a named test asserts what its name claims

counting.base_and_head_from: the exact review tuple, never a moving ref
counting.changed_files: every changed path, including generated files and the lockfile; a rename or copy counts both source and destination
counting.total_reviewed_diff_lines: additions plus deletions across every text file; only lockfile lines may be excluded
counting.binary_files: fail closed; a binary change is never counted as zero lines
counting.per_file_line_cap: none exists and none may be inferred

prohibited_evasions: placing a normative requirement in a file outside normative_markdown_paths
generating content to stay under the handwritten limit
bundling rules that can change independently into one declared concept
omitting a model from the declared concept list

concepts: exact review identity and CI identity

stage_registry.amendment: adding, removing or reordering a stage is a constitutional amendment requiring a new semantic review and a Founder decision

conditional_extension_rules: permitted only where the first round's findings are repairable within the already-approved specification
the conditional round reviews the exact new review tuple
the maximum number of completed verdicts is never exceeded and there is no third round
a specification gap stops immediately and returns to the Founder
a no-verdict invocation consumes no completed round and is not retried automatically
a CLEAN or APPROVE verdict at an old tuple never carries to a new one

stop_rules.action: stop and return to the Founder, whatever budget remains; never patched in-round

stop_rules.trigger: budget exhausted with a blocker or high outstanding
stop_rules.action: hard stop, return to the Founder

merge_conditions: zero blocker and zero high, judged as the aggregate of unresolved findings on the tuple
every medium and low carries a named Founder disposition; there is no default
required checks green at the reviewed head

closure_routes.name: structural or executable
requires: an artifact that fails at the pre-fix commit, with its exact command and result
the same artifact passing at the fix commit, with its exact command and result
a mutation control that removes or inverts the load-bearing mechanism and states which mechanism it removed, where such a mechanism exists

closure_routes.name: change detection
requires: exact base, head, merge-base, tree and diff identity
comparison against the external review tuple
no self-approval by the pull request presenting it

closure_routes.name: semantic or specification
requires: the same immutable finding identifier and content digest
an independent reviewer verdict at that exact head explicitly confirming the finding is resolved
a Founder decision or disposition bound to that tuple

asserted_not_proven.meaning: a closure missing the evidence its own proof class requires
asserted_not_proven.never_applies_because: no program can test a purely semantic claim

security_safe_evidence_forms: immutable digest of the restricted artifact
public_text_rule: public specification text, pull request bodies and reviewer briefs carry only safe characterisations and never restate a security payload, exploit input or reproduction script
ci_requirements: assert git rev-parse HEAD equals the event head sha
fetch the declared base and assert the merge-base equals the reviewed base
record the head tree sha and the diff identity as evidence
run with minimal read-only permissions and no secrets
never describe the default synthetic merge checkout as exact-head CI
never rely on a provider identifier being monotonically ordered

reviewer_capacity.scope: one authority domain: one authoritative database and the host that owns it
reviewer_capacity.measured_in: actually in-flight invocations, not active claim records
reviewer_capacity.lost_owner: an invocation whose owner is lost keeps occupying capacity until proved terminal, cancellation confirmed, or a probe confirms it is not running
reviewer_capacity.no_probe_no_cancel: fails closed and holds capacity indefinitely
reviewer_capacity.independence: the reviewer is a principal distinct from the principal that produced the change

gates.evaluates: whether all nineteen stages are complete in order
whether real provider implementation may begin
requires: each deferred decision answered by an approved resolution carrying an outcome, a content reference and a content version

non_waivable: one implementation pull request per lane

per_stage: it is reviewed at its exact review tuple within budget
the Founder dispositions every finding and authorises the merge
the checkpoint pull request merges and closes
only then may that stage's implementation pull request open

asset_disposition_rules: reused material is reviewed again in the stage that reintroduces it; a prior review of a different pull request is not a review of this one
